title: Split-flap board
suits: travel, mobility, logistics and freight, scheduling, booking, events and anything about time, routes or arrivals

params.--field: the station wall (vermilion by default; any colour or gradient)
params.--brand: the mark's colour in its flap (used if it reads on the board, 3:1)
params.--brand-2: fallback mark colour; else the flap ink
params.--flap-board / --flap-top / --flap-bot /: the near-black board, its two flap halves and the characters (independent of the wall, so they always read)
params.--flap-cw: maximum flap width (shrinks so long names fit 1700 px)
params.__MARK__: stroke paths in a 24 x 24 box; it lands in its own flap

details: the board is already hanging, blank, before the press: an empty station waiting for the update
every flap spins through its drum in drum order (blank, A–Z, 0–9, -, .), so the clatter looks mechanical, not random
each flap starts a hair after its left neighbour, so the board ripples into motion
flaps land left to right; the timing is solved per flap so each reaches its letter exactly on schedule
the final flap of each letter bounces a hair off its stop and settles
one flap (about 60% along the word) lands a beat late
the falling half darkens as it turns away from the light; the rising half brightens as it lands
the falling flap shades the new top half, and the old bottom darkens as it is covered
a soft shadow under every flap, a dark hinge line and two metal hinge pins per flap
the housing shivers a fraction of a pixel while the flaps clatter and goes still when the last one lands
the mark has its own flap and briefly passes through other flaps as part of the drum
the board hangs from two rods with clamp brackets; a lamp above lights the wall and the board's top edge
enamel wall panels with faint joints
at rest, every 14 s the last blank flap shuffles once as if the board is updating
any character the name needs (an ampersand, an accent) is added to the drum
on a near-black wall a faint rim lifts the board off the wall
